title: GPU surge safety and contract conversion workpad — Nov 2026
content:
Purpose:
This workpad is an operational planning sheet for two concurrent needs: (1) convert a subset of multi-year reserved contracts into flexible tranche-allocations for Q1–Q3 2027, and (2) define a surge-safety cushion and regional swap rules for Dedicated customers to avoid SLA impact during regional capacity stress.

Context / constraints (short):
- We have a mix of c5-like and h100-like commitments across regions (NA, EU, APAC). Some contracts are fixed-GPU type; others are convertible within a family (H100 -> H100-q8/4/2 variants).
- Goal: preserve customer throughput SLAs while freeing 8–12% of peak capacity to serve spot and hosted API spikes.
- Business asks: avoid breaking contracts, minimize penalty exposure, and give Sales a productized "convert + buffer" offering for customers that want temporary peak coverage.
- Ops objective: build predictable fallback rules and an automated reconciliation report (daily) for allocations vs actual utilization.

Assumptions and definitions (operational):
- "Committed GPU-hour" = contracted GPU * committed hours per month (standardized to 30d months).
- Cushion target = 10% of committed on active contracts per region (adjustable by region).
- Utilization goal = 75% average utilization across Dedicated fleet (we size to 75% to allow short-term bursts).
- Convertible tranche = portion of a contract flagged as "soft-slashable" (can be reallocated with 30d notice) without SLA breach if swap rules applied.

Quick reference formulas (for sheet automation):
- region_cushion = round_up(total_committed_gpu * cushion_target_pct)
- available_for_spot = physical_capacity - sum(active_dedicated_allocations) - reserved_cushion_pool
- contract_headroom = max(0, contracted_gpu - observed_avg_usage_last_7d)

High-level scenario sketches:
1) Baseline — no conversion
   - Cushion by region: NA 10%, EU 8%, APAC 12% (APAC higher due to arrival patterns).
   - Peak-day risk: if hosting API surge consumes > 6% of regional capacity, start soft fallback sequence (route low-priority traffic to compatible lower-precision variants).

2) Conversion plan — targeted contracts (pilot)
   - Candidates: 3 enterprise contracts (C-183, C-207, C-214) with > 6 months remaining and allow convertible-hours clause in SOW.
   - Proposed conversion: move 20% of each contract into a convertible tranche for 6 months. Exchange rules: 30d notice for reconversion, no penalty if conversion used <= 2 months per rolling 6m window.

3) Surge reallocation (emergency flow)
   - Trigger: sustained regional overload > 95% physical occupancy for 10m with 99th p99 latency > SLO.
   - Steps: (a) route compatible Dedicated workloads to partner-region (if customer consented), (b) pull from convertible tranches (FIFO by age), (c) spin temporary burst nodes (if cloud capacity available), (d) notify CS/Customer with reason + ETA.

Allocation snapshot (example numbers — use this as template):

| Contract | Region | Committed GPUs | Convertible tranche | Avg 7d use | Headroom | Notes |
| C-183 | NA | 120 | 24 | 88 | 32 | candidate — has convertible clause |
| C-207 | EU | 80 | 16 | 60 | 20 | supports regional swap to NA |
| C-214 | APAC | 64 | 12 | 52 | 12 | shorten notice ok (15d) — needs approval |
| Internal-hosted-spot | NA | 40 | 0 | 25 | 15 | non-contract — ephemeral pool |

Operational runbook (condensed):
- Daily morning digest (08:00 PST): compute per-region "commitment delta" = physical_capacity - (allocated_committed + cushion_target). If delta < 0 => schedule mitigation ticket.
- Weekly reconciliation (Mon): compare contract_headroom sum vs available_for_spot. If headroom < 10% long-run, prepare capacity request for procurement meeting.
- Escalation ladder: on trigger -> SRE oncall -> infra lead (Raj) -> CS lead (Diego) -> sales rep of impacted contracts. Communication template in CONFLUENCE link.

Customer-facing product mechanic (proposal sketch):
- "Flex-Tranche" add-on: customers purchase a convertible tranche (X GPUs) which can be temporarily reallocated to regional pool for 30d increments. In return they get credit (1.5% monthly) and SLA guarantee of reconversion within 30d.
- Pricing note: credit must be priced to offset lost committed revenue (approx 60–70% of committed rate) but keep product attractive vs full host credit. Need finance input.

Risk map and open decisions: (short bullets)
- Legal: the exact penalty and notification windows in existing SOWs — need legal signoff for automatic tranche cutover. (Action: Priya to pull 10 impacted SOWs and flag clause types.)
- Observability: need per-tenant 1m granularity usage metric to make reversible decisions without SLA hits. Current datapipeline has 5m granularity for dedicated; 1m target by Dec 2026. (Action: Lina)
- Accounting: how to handle revenue recognition and credit accrual for Flex-Tranche — finance touchpoint required. (Action: schedule with Finance ops)
- Customer consent model: implicit vs explicit consent for region swap. Default: opt-in via contract amendment. (Action: CS to draft amendment language.)

Mini-simulations (back-of-envelope) — pilot cohort (C-183, C-207, C-214) if we convert 20% each: 
- freed GPUs: 24 + 16 + 12 = 52 GPUs
- regional cushion target used: NA 12 by C-183 conversion contributes 24 -> net NA freed = 12 (partial), EU freed = 0 net if conversions held in EU, APAC freed = 12.
- expected additional spot capacity for hosted API ~ 40–45 GPUs after cushion accounted.
- risk: if reconversion demand spikes simultaneously in NA and EU, we could hit cross-region constraints; need pre-agreed reroute allowances.

Quick checklist for pilot rollout (timeline 8 weeks):
- Week 0: legal + finance review of terms (Priya / Finance)
- Week 1: instrument per-tenant 1m telemetry (Lina / infra infra) — fallback to 5m if impossible
- Week 2–3: CS outreach + contract amendments signed (Diego / CS)
- Week 4: enable convertible tranches in billing system and allocation engine (Raj / infra eng)
- Week 5: run a planned stress test in region (internal traffic) — measure reconversion latency
- Week 6–8: monitor pilot; decide go/no-go for broader productization

Notes to self / loose thoughts (informal):
- We should consider a "grace reserve" that is separate from cushion — something like a 4–6 GPU per region that can be used to avoid noisy-neighbor thrash while convertible tranches rehydrate.
- Possibility: allow customers to specify allowed fallback target regions (white-list) in UI to speed automated failover.
- Explore automated billing credit ledger that amortizes credit while tranche is active; keep credits visible on monthly invoice.

Open questions for next meeting (priority order):
1) Legal clause template for convertible tranches (high)
2) Finance model for credit pricing and revenue leakage calculation (high)
3) Do we allow swap of GPU generations (H100 <-> H100-q8) without notice? operationally we can, but check quality implications (medium)
4) Default cushion % by contract size band (small/medium/large) — propose banding rather than flat %.

Attachments / reference tables to paste into final sheet: (placeholders)
- Per-region physical capacity table (CSV) — TODO: Lina to attach current snapshot
- Pilot contract SOW excerpts — Priya
- Daily digest template (Slack + email) — Diego

— end of workpad —

(rough, half-formed; this is intended as a practical planning artifact that will be iterated in the infra squad and shared with CS/legal/finance for pilot scoping.)
